blocks.content: A startup probe exists specifically for applications with a genuinely slow startup, disabling liveness and readiness checks until it succeeds once, preventing an impatient liveness probe from killing an app that simply needed more time to boot.

Some applications, particularly legacy systems or ones performing heavy initialization work, genuinely take a long time to become ready, far longer than a typical liveness probe's tolerance, a startup probe is built specifically for this case.

blocks.alt: A dedicated tool for applications that legitimately need real time to boot

blocks.content: 2. Suspending Liveness and Readiness Until It Succeeds
blocks.text: 2. Suspending Liveness and Readiness Until It Succeeds

blocks.content: While a startup probe is defined and has not yet succeeded, both the liveness and readiness probes are held off entirely, only once the startup probe genuinely succeeds do those other two checks even begin running.

blocks.alt: Other health checks paused, until startup genuinely confirms the app is up

blocks.content: Without a startup probe, a liveness probe configured for a normal, fast-starting app would repeatedly fail during a slow app's legitimate boot process, and kubelet would kill and restart it, over and over, before it ever had a real chance to finish starting.

blocks.alt: The exact failure mode this probe type is specifically designed to prevent

blocks.content: The moment a startup probe succeeds, even just once, its job is done, liveness and readiness probes take over from that point forward, behaving exactly as they would for any ordinary container.

blocks.alt: A one-time gate, after which normal health checking resumes as usual

blocks.content: A legacy Java application with a genuinely slow, multi-minute startup sequence is a textbook case, a generous startup probe gives it the real time it needs, without weakening the liveness probe's sensitivity once the app is actually running normally.

blocks.alt: A genuine multi-minute boot, given the patience it actually needs

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A startup probe holds off liveness and readiness checks until it succeeds once, protecting genuinely slow-starting applications from being killed prematurely.
Once it succeeds, liveness and readiness take over normally, this is a one-time gate for startup, not a permanent replacement for the other two probe types.
